liebermann.notes: A separately foliated paper booklet with William Somner's transcript of Anglo-Saxon laws, incomplete and misbound (after 1705 the Pseudo-Evangelium Nicodemi was bound behind it); it preserves Af to 38, Ine from 54, II As 1–15 and II Eg 4–III Eg 7,2, from an exemplar that did not have these gaps; the source is unnamed. For Eg it follows with Ld a common source ls (which with G follows another, gls, perhaps direct from the original), both posited by Liebermann; for II As it derives, against H B (Ld), from sq; for Af–Ine it follows ls and gls.

entries.text_de: Papierheft mit William Somner’s1 Abschrift Angelsächsischer Gesetze, in Canterbury Cathedral library B 2 n. 8 ist ein besonders foliirtes Heft; das Af Vorhergehende hat keine Beziehung dazu. Jetzt, aber erst nach 17052, dahinter gebunden ist Pseudo-evangelium Nicodemi, abgeschrieben aus Bibl. publ. Univ. Cantabrig. Das Heft ist lückenhaft und falsch gebunden. Es sollte folgen: f. 1; 2 ff.; 1b; 5; 7—16; es fehlen mindestens 2 Folien; 21—24; 17—20; fehlen Folien; 6. Erhalten ist: f. 1—5. 7—16 Af bis 38, u. S. 16—7032; f. 21—24 Ine von 54 ab, u. S. 11231—22; f. 17—20 II As 1—15, u. S. 150—58, Sp. 3**; f. 6 II Eg 4—III 7, 2, u. S. 19810—20420. Diese Lücken hatte die Vorlage nicht, da am unteren Rande der Seiten, wo jetzt Text abbricht, noch Rubrik für Folgendes vorgeschrieben ist. Die Quelle ist nicht genannt. Für Eg folgt sie mit Ld einem verlorenen ls, das mit G einem verlorenen gls folgte. Dies kann, neben adg, vom Original direct stammen. Für II As fliesst sie, gegen H B (Ld), aus sq, einer mit Quadr. gemeinsamen Vorlage, die von osq, einer dieser mit Ot gemeinsamen Quelle, stammt. Für Af-Ine folgt So ebenfalls ls und dieses mit G wieder gls.
entries.text_en: A paper booklet with William Somner’s1 transcript of Anglo-Saxon laws; in Canterbury Cathedral library B 2 n. 8 it is a separately foliated booklet; what precedes Af has no connection with it. Now, but only after 17052, the Pseudo-evangelium Nicodemi, copied from Bibl. publ. Univ. Cantabrig., is bound in behind it. The booklet is defective and wrongly bound. The order should be: f. 1; 2 ff.; 1b; 5; 7—16; at least 2 folios are missing; 21—24; 17—20; folios missing; 6. What survives is: f. 1—5. 7—16 Af to 38, below, p. 16—7032; f. 21—24 Ine from 54 onwards, below, p. 11231—22; f. 17—20 II As 1—15, below, pp. 150—58, col. 3**; f. 6 II Eg 4—III 7, 2, below, p. 19810—20420. The exemplar did not have these gaps, since at the bottom margin of the pages, where the text now breaks off, a rubric for what follows is still written in advance. The source is not named. For Eg it follows, together with Ld, a lost ls, which together with G followed a lost gls. This may, alongside adg, derive directly from the original. For II As it derives, as against H B (Ld), from sq, an exemplar shared with Quadr., which descends from osq, a source shared by the latter with Ot. For Af-Ine So likewise follows ls, and this in turn, with G, follows gls.

notes.text_de: Die Handschrift 17. Jhs. identificirte mir Dr. Sheppard.
notes.text_en: The 17th-century hand was identified for me by Dr. Sheppard.

notes.text_de: Wanley (bei Hickes Thes. ling. sept. III 271) erwähnt nur letzteres. Wäre, was er 270 Schedae solutae, m. G. Lambardi: Aelfredi leges nennt, mit So identisch, so hätte er die Hand ein Jahrhundert zu alt erachtet.
notes.text_en: Wanley (in Hickes Thes. ling. sept. III 271) mentions only the latter. If what he calls on 270 Schedae solutae, m. G. Lambardi: Aelfredi leges were identical with So, he would have judged the hand a century too old.

transcription.doubts: Superscripts 32, 31, 10, 20 are line references, not footnote marks. 'das Af Vorhergehende': 'Af' is in roman (not bold) here. 'Sp. 3**' = column 3 (double asterisk as printed). 'Somner's', 'Canterbury' letter-spaced. 'ls' could be read 'Is' but is the lost-MS siglum ls (lowercase l).

wormald.wormald_origin: A Nowell transcript, later owned by William Somner in the 17th century; Nowell's authorship discovered by Carl Berkhout (p. 262 n. 380).
wormald.laws: II–III Eg (p. 262); also among the Nowell transcripts behind Lambarde's Grately/Exeter and Alfred–Ine texts (p. 262), and contains Af 8 (p. 171 n. 38). Wormald does not list its contents in full (guide: Af, Ine, II As, II Eg, III Eg).
wormald.laws_liebermann: Af, Ine, II As, II Eg, III Eg
wormald.overview: A transcript of Anglo-Saxon laws that Liebermann ascribed to the seventeenth-century antiquary William Somner, its later owner, and thought to depend on lost manuscripts. It is in fact Laurence Nowell's work: for Edgar an editorial version based on Nero A.i(A), close to but not the same as what Lambarde printed, and it is also one of the working copies behind Lambarde's texts of Æthelstan and Alfred–Ine. Its readings therefore carry no independent authority.
wormald.liebermann_superseded: Liebermann (Gesetze I, p. xl) attributed this transcript to William Somner and thought it drew on one or more lost manuscripts; Wormald (p. 262 and n. 380, after Berkhout) shows it is a Nowell editorial exercise, for Edgar based on Nero A.i(A), with no independent textual authority (cf. p. 171 n. 38).
wormald.key_quote: 'It was in fact another Nowell editorial exercise, based on Nero A.i(A), and not what was printed by Lambarde' (p. 262)
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: the guide's So entry should be corrected: the hand is Laurence Nowell's (16th century), not Somner's; Somner was its 17th-century owner. Guide gives 'B 2 no. 8'; Wormald 'MS Lit. B.2'. Wormald's 'based on Nero A.i(A)' is said of the Edgar text; the basis for its Af–Ine and II As is not stated. At p. 171 n. 38 Wormald notes that Liebermann used 'Somner's' text to support the Parker MS reading at Af 8, but holds that it has no textual authority.
